title: When the Harvest Fails, Whose Business Fails First

body.en: Adjoa buys tomatoes and peppers from farmers near her town and resells them at the market — it's how she has supported her household for eleven years. This season, an erratic rainy season meant two of her regular farmers lost most of their crop. The tomatoes that did survive cost nearly double what she used to pay. Adjoa raised her prices too, but her regular customers started buying less, and some stopped coming altogether. She is now considering a loan just to keep her stall running until prices settle. Her business didn't fail because of anything she did — it's being squeezed by a harvest that failed somewhere else entirely.

followUpQuestion: How did a change in the weather end up threatening Adjoa's income, even though she isn't a farmer herself?
